name: FlexFactor
historical_purpose: A local dual-provider refactorer that grew into a managed purpose-driven audit, repair, verification, and publication system.
purpose: Improve an owner's software without turning generated code, partial execution, or a stranded branch into false success: understand why the target exists, account for the complete repository, run and attempt to break relevant behavior, retain only independently verified corrections, preserve owner work and sensitive source, and prove the exact reviewed revision on the authoritative remote default branch.

current_behavior.text: One durable orchestrator accepts 1 through 30 targets and admits exactly one at a time.
Audit and Production Ready run at most six semantic passes: the whole repository first, a top-three competitor capability gate, then only the immediately preceding verified edit delta.
Every model call uses one strongest-paid-to-free availability ladder; legacy provider, paid/free, and economy flags cannot select another production path.
All ladder instances in one run share author-family identity and reviewer calls fail closed unless a family that authored none of the candidate is available.
Intermediate checkpoints stay local; completion after a change requires green executable and evidence gates, complete exact-commit independent review, and remote-default ancestry proof for that SHA.

Android persists a 30-target sequential queue; the cloud atomically claims each request UUID, recovers an existing GitHub workflow instead of duplicating dispatch after a crash, and removes phone-supplied secrets at terminal status.

aspirations.text: OS-enforced Windows network isolation in addition to current process-tree and resource controls.

users.text: Owners running Refactor, Scout, Audit, or Production Ready on their repositories from the signed Android app, desktop launchers, or CLI.
Supervisors consuming exit codes, queue receipts, run manifests, error ledgers, and evidence bundles.

outcomes.text: Verified corrections land on the authoritative remote default branch without force-push and owner WIP is restored by fingerprint.
Every incomplete provider, verification, review, publication, or release condition remains visible as BLOCKED or IN PROGRESS.

workflows.text: Audit: publication preflight, inventory and purpose, whole-repository pass 1, top-three competitor gate, exact-delta passes 2 through 6, native and browser verification, evidence, independent exact-commit review, publication, and remote-default proof.
Production Ready executes the Audit workflow with its full readiness rubric and unattended production defaults.
Scout profiles and researches improvements; mutation requires explicit Scout authorization and the same verification and publication contract.
Refactor rewrites selected files toward explicit goals and accepts no change until project verification, independent review, and publication prove it.

invariants.text: No review-only or dry-run escape exists in Audit or Production Ready.
A verifier outage leaves the target unchanged and creates no successful publication.
Owner WIP never becomes an ancestor of a FlexFactor-published branch.
Partial output never authorizes clean, ready, approval, commit publication, or merge.
A host capability that is not enforced is named as best effort, never claimed as containment.
Every claimed gate must have run; unknown and unavailable are not passes.
A changed run cannot exit successfully until the exact reviewed SHA is proven on the authoritative remote default branch.
No reviewer from any candidate author family can certify the final commit.

acceptance_criteria: A. The ordered target queue contains at most 30 items and no two targets overlap.
B. Pass 1 covers the complete repository and passes 2 through 6 exactly equal the preceding verified edit delta.
C. The top three corroborated competitors are considered after pass 1 and before pass 2.
D. One best-available ladder consumes strongest paid or subscription capacity before lower paid and then free or local capacity.
E. Every target-controlled install, build, test, or server command crosses the execution broker.
F. Every tracked or relevant file is analyzed, analyzed in complete chunks, or blocked with a reason.
G. Purpose evidence cites sources, contradictions, unknowns, and confidence before purpose-driven mutation.
H. Partial or malformed structured output cannot authorize a clean or approval verdict.
I. Every retained correction passes the target's real build and strongest project suite.
J. Every model family that authored candidate content is excluded from final-review selection.
K. The independent final review accounts for the complete exact-commit patch in content-addressed chunks.
L. A HEAD movement after review revokes approval.
M. Changed-file rescan, blast radius, secret evidence, and direct behavior coverage are complete or named blockers.
N. Applicable live UI journeys account for roles, routes, controls, forms, accessibility, and performance.
O. Owner WIP is captured outside candidate ancestry and restored only on fingerprint equality.
P. Intermediate commits never push and FlexFactor never force-pushes.
Q. A protected branch uses a normal pull request and remains incomplete until merged.
R. A fresh fetch proves the exact reviewed SHA is reachable from the authoritative remote default branch.
S. The installed wheel, managed cloud, signed Android APK, and source runtime all identify the matching release.
T. Production readiness requires merged main, green exact-SHA CI, deployed cloud, published signed APK, and live end-to-end proof.

gaps.text: Windows raw-socket network isolation is best effort rather than OS enforced.

evidence.excerpt: Best-available ladder and shared strict author-family exclusion.
Four modes, mutation preflight, verification, review, and exact-default-branch publication.
Managed OAuth, atomic idempotent dispatch, ephemeral provider-secret cleanup, artifacts, and steering.
Governing purpose and production completion contract.
Managed sign-in, sequential dispatch, crash recovery, and fail-closed durable queue advancement.
Executable gate ledger in which unavailable and not-run gates cannot be counted as passes.

false_substitutes: A build passing without the strongest project suite.
An HTTP health response without authenticated workflow proof.
Tests existing without being executed on the exact candidate.
A commit or pull request existing without independent verification.
Module import being counted as direct function execution.
Partial or salvaged model output being treated as complete.
Best-effort environment poisoning being called OS containment.
A checkpoint existing without SHA and policy verification.
